newsitem.title: UK: Pru mulls legal action on funds-paper.
newsitem.headline: Pru mulls legal action on funds-paper.

text.p: Prudential Corp Plc is considering legal action against Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to establish ownership over three billion pounds ($4.92 billion) of surplus insurance funds, the Times reported on Friday.
The undistributed surplus, called "orphan assets", arises where the total available to pay out to policy holders exceeds estimates of the funds' maximum liabilities.
The question of who owns the surplus funds has been a matter of protracted debate between individual insurers and the DTI.

Prudential, which earlier this week launched a 1.9 billion pounds ($3.12 billion) bid for life insurer Scottish Amicable, said in May 1996 that talks with the DTI would probably take 12 months to complete.
But Prudential's chief executive, Sir Peter Davis, was understood to be losing patience with the DTI, the Times said.
The newspaper, which named no sources, said Prudential declined to comment on its report.
